name: a cycle refused at link time
about: A link that would close a loop is refused when it is made, and so are links to a port that does not exist or that points the wrong way.
notes: Links are made in order. l1 a to b and l2 b to c are fine.
l3 c to a closes a, b, c, a and is refused: cycle.
l4 a to a is the smallest cycle there is and is refused: cycle.
l5 names port d, which was never declared: unknown-port.
l6 starts at out1, which is an output only: direction.
Events: a reaches b through l1, b reaches c through l2, and c reaches nothing because l3 does not exist.
The core does not feed what it writes to a port back in as that port's input, so the note at b does not travel on to c by itself.
